title: Trace the production path before crediting a local fix or speedup
applies_when: A helper, intermediate CSV or kernel microbenchmark changes, but the observable consumer result, backend dispatch or share of the target workload is uncertain.
lesson: Trace representative requests to the implementation and consumer that actually run. A baseline-failing helper test need not demonstrate a user-visible failure: downstream normalization can already restore the required result. For config deduplication, compare selected configs and errors after the real loader, not only intermediate CSV row counts. Before crediting a parser microbenchmark, exercise request-local initialization and caller gates: prefilled reasoning, already-ended state or an explicit constrain-from-start policy can bypass the optimized helper. Count actual helper calls separately from timing; a passed observation of zero calls is a no-benefit path, not accelerated execution. Check whether an existing correctness repair changes the algorithm or removes the measured work; remeasure against it instead of carrying forward obsolete ratios. Estimate how much elapsed time a component can remove before expanding optimization work. An Amdahl estimate needs a measured non-overlapping time share and unchanged residual work; inclusive profiler totals are not automatically that share. Confirm the eventual result in the target workload.
avoid_when: An intermediate artifact or public helper can have its own documented contract; cleanup can be valuable when honestly scoped or backed by measured file/parse cost. One unaffected loader does not prove all consumers safe. Do not treat a configuration flag as execution evidence, invent a missing time share, or apply a universal minimum gain. A component harness that skips manager construction, grammar/backend setup or model generation is not full serving qualification. Supporting an existing repair with a current-main reproduction does not validate its entire implementation or justify a competing PR. Amdahl's simple serial model needs adjustment when overlap, concurrency or bottlenecks change.

evidence.note: Official guidance supports realistic workload profiling and scope-limited speedup bounds. It does not establish reachability or a measured gain for any particular candidate.

Closed after maintainer feedback: the missing-untuned branch's exact-row deduplication changes temporary CSV row counts, but the cited MXFP8 route already deduplicates in get_CKGEMM_config. Four host-only production-method comparisons preserve selected configs/errors. AST extraction isolates the lock and hardware queries; this is not full AITER/ROCm qualification or an all-consumer safety claim.

Scope-corrected atomic MiniMax marker proposal retains historical official-tokenizer predicate-only ratios. Current473cc8ec raw-source two-arm CPU observations through real Request and manager bounds give384helper calls over128body tokens in the default mode, zero in thinking-enabled/already-ended/constrain-in-reasoning modes; four observations pass per arm. Manager __new__ and a contract tokenizer limit this to component reachability, not current timing, full serving or general speedup.

Independent current-main observation supports the existing author's thinking-enabled gate issue: bounds remain unconstrained after the closing marker, with or without the atomic lookup patch. This is not qualification of the peer's incremental/speculative cache logic, live grammar/model evidence or a new discovery. The existing repair may remove the historical full-history scan, requiring new performance comparisons.
